input.quote: Neither Party may assign, transfer or subcontract any rights or duties under this Agreement without prior written approval by the other Party. MSL may assign or subcontract all or any part of this Agreement to any MSL Related Company with IBM's prior written consent which shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed.
input.rationale: Section 16.2 imposes a flat consent requirement on both Parties with no carve-out permitting IBM to assign to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, and no reasonableness standard on the consent IBM must obtain (the reasonableness qualifier is given only to MSL's Related Company assignments). That is the walk-away case in the rule — a blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out — and it also fails the fallback, which requires at minimum a mutual right to assign to successors on written notice with consent otherwise not unreasonably withheld. Section 16.5 (Sale or Merger) is favourable to us: it binds only MSL, requiring notice and assumption by any successor, and gives MSL no termination or re-pricing right on an IBM change of control, so no change-of-control right needs deletion; our redline confirms this expressly for the avoidance of doubt. The redline makes the minimum edit to reach the preferred position: an IBM affiliate/successor carve-out on notice plus a reasonableness standard, leaving MSL's existing restrictions and subcontracting notice duties intact.

proposal.summary: Add IBM affiliate/successor assignment carve-out and a reasonableness standard to the mutual consent requirement in § 16.2.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added an affiliate and successor carve-out so that IBM may assign to a group company or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets on notice, and made the consent standard reasonable; our playbook does not accept a blanket bar on customer assignment with no M&A carve-out. MSL's consent obligations and the existing MSL restrictions are unchanged.

ops.oldText: Neither Party may assign, transfer or subcontract any rights or duties under this Agreement without prior written approval by the other Party.
ops.newText: Except as expressly provided below, neither Party may assign, transfer or subcontract any rights or duties under this Agreement without prior written approval by the other Party, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed. Notwithstanding the foregoing, IBM may assign or transfer this Agreement, in whole or in part, without MSL's consent to any entity controlling, controlled by or under common control with IBM, or to any successor in interest by way of merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of the assets or business to which this Agreement relates, upon written notice to MSL, and no such event shall give MSL any right to terminate, suspend or re-price this Agreement.
